section_summary: This section opens with a continuing table of Japanese wartime commodity requirements and production, followed by a map of strategic commodities. Telegrams from Chungking discuss Japanese oil production in the Netherlands East Indies, summarize economic news from monitored Japanese broadcasts, and track a microfilmed booklet on Japanese diplomacy. A despatch and its enclosure provide a much longer, region-by-region compilation of broadcast reports on production, trade, transport, finance, and administration.

subfiles.title: Japanese requirements and production of fibers and foodstuffs by producing region, 1943
subfiles.about: Compares Japanese requirements, stocks, and regional production of fibers and foodstuffs.
subfiles.summary: A continuing table estimates Japanese requirements and available production of cotton, other fibers, oils, rice, soybeans, sugar, and wheat. It distinguishes Japan’s home production from supplies in occupied or controlled regions and comments on shortages and surpluses.

subfiles.title: Strategic commodities in the inner and outer zone
subfiles.about: Maps strategic commodity production across Japan’s inner and outer zones.
subfiles.summary: A Board of Economic Warfare map identifies strategic commodities, including electric power, pig iron, and steel, across Japan and surrounding zones.

subfiles.title: Chungking telegram on Japanese oil production
subfiles.about: Reports a Dutch estimate of Japanese oil output in North Borneo and the East Indies.
subfiles.summary: Dutch officials estimate output at about six million barrels annually, roughly one-tenth of prewar production.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Chungking telegram 958
subfiles.about: Restates the Dutch assessment of Japanese oil production.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase explains that Dutch officials doubted Japan could quickly raise annual output to sixty million barrels.

subfiles.title: Request for estimate of Japanese oil from other sources
subfiles.about: Requests an estimate of oil Japan needs from other sources if East Indies output is six million barrels annually.
subfiles.summary: Stone asks the embassy to estimate production from other sources required to meet current Japanese oil consumption.

subfiles.title: Chungking telegram 964: economic news from Japanese broadcasts
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, Washington; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Summarizes monitored Japanese economic broadcasts from May 26 through June 15.
subfiles.summary: Thirty-one items cover Japanese budgets, industrial substitution, shipping, metals, communications, and trade. Reports from Manchuria and occupied China address mines, agriculture, banking, food control, and transport. Items from Southeast Asia describe sugar, rubber, cotton, copper, and Indochinese budgets.

subfiles.title: Chungking telegram 978 on microfilmed diplomacy booklet
subfiles.about: Explains the second microfilming of a Japanese diplomacy booklet.
subfiles.summary: The embassy holds the booklet while Washington inspects a clearer microfilm copy.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Chungking telegram 978
subfiles.about: Restates the handling of the microfilmed Japanese diplomacy booklet.
subfiles.summary: A clearer copy was submitted to INDEC; originals could follow by pouch if requested.

subfiles.title: Copy of Chungking telegram 978
subfiles.about: Records the embassy’s explanation of the duplicate microfilm submission.
subfiles.summary: The embassy awaits inspection of the second microfilm before sending original publications.

subfiles.title: Additional copy of Chungking telegram 978
subfiles.about: Duplicates the telegram about microfilming and retaining the diplomacy booklet.
subfiles.summary: Another copy records the second microfilm submission and possible forwarding of originals.

subfiles.title: Despatch 1245: Economic material from Japanese broadcasts
subfiles.from: George Atcheson Jr., American Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: Forwards fuller broadcast reports and additional items to the Department of State.
subfiles.summary: The cover letter explains the Chinese and American monitoring sources used for its enclosure.

subfiles.title: Contents of economic material from Japanese broadcasts
subfiles.about: Indexes broadcast reports by region and item number.
subfiles.summary: The contents list groups reports under Japan, Manchuria, occupied China, Hong Kong, the Philippines, the East Indies, Malaya, Indochina, Thailand, and Burma.

subfiles.title: Enclosure 1 to despatch 1245: Economic items selected from radio broadcasts
subfiles.to: Department of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Provides detailed translations and summaries of monitored Japanese and Nanking-regime economic broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: The report expands earlier telegram summaries and adds reports of possible interest to the Board of Economic Warfare. Items through page 54 describe Japanese mobilization plans, industrial inventions, trade organization, mining, agriculture, transport, currency controls, and production across occupied territories. The final pages address Chinese famine relief, trade agreements, and Japanese and French concessions in China; the enclosure continues beyond this section.
